STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white plate with a raised rim band and a flat centre, no inner bowl wall. It is a square plate with rounded corners. Flat plate (square).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: square plates are 20-30 cm. The plate looks medium-large relative to the food, so I estimate about 25 cm.
b) Reference cue: the scrambled egg and melon cubes are roughly 2-3 cm pieces. The plate spans about 3.5 to 4 of the 5.5 cm eggs... more practically, the melon cubes (about 2.5-3 cm) fill about 1/8 of the width each, which puts the width near 24-26 cm.
Reconciled width: 25 cm. Area = 625 cm2.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Sweet potato cubes: they cover roughly the lower-left quadrant, about 22% of the plate area = 137 cm2. Piled about 2.5 cm thick (a pile of chunky pieces, mound averages about half of ~4-5 cm peak). Volume = 137 x 2.2 = 301 ml. Bulk density for cooked roasted vegetable ~0.8 g/ml gives ~240 g.
- Scrambled egg: upper-left, about 14% = 88 cm2, mound about 2 cm average. Volume = 176 ml x 0.8 = 141 g.
- Bacon: right-centre, about 8% = 50 cm2, flat layer 0.5 cm. Volume = 25 ml x 1.0 = 25 g.
- Melon (cantaloupe/honeydew) cubes: right and lower-right, about 10% = 63 cm2, layer about 2 cm. Volume = 126 ml x 0.6 = 76 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No separate base layer is visible; the plate is essentially a single layer of items, so no extra hidden items are added.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Sweet potato, roasted: about 110 kcal/100 g (oil-roasted slightly higher, use 130).
- Scrambled egg with milk and butter: about 150 kcal/100 g.
- Bacon, cooked: about 540 kcal/100 g.
- Cantaloupe/honeydew melon: about 35 kcal/100 g.

Totals: about 240 + 141 + 25 + 76 = 482 g; energy roughly 312 + 212 + 135 + 27 = about 690 kcal.
